title: "Gm top chickens": the record holder's greeting and the posts it drew (Sun 15 Nov)
summary: On Sun 15 Nov at 15:39Z, an hour and a half after that day's result, @cee.wtf (the record holder and Saturday's winner) posted "Gm top chickens" (53 likes, 8 replies, 3 quotes). Sunday's winner, @thebadcode.com, replied "gm" with a chicken emoji. Two other members replied "gm". Three members quoted the post. @jefferyharrell.bsky.social, within a minute: "Gm to all my chickens, top, middle and bottom." followed by "</virtue-signal>" (15 likes). @shimmermathlabs.com, an hour later: "if you quote post a top chicken post you become a bottom chicken, i don't make the rules" (36 likes). The third quote is left out (see sensitive). Earlier the same day, at 00:49Z, @catblanketflower.yuwakisa.com had posted "someday I will be Top Chicken" (6 likes).
couldShow: The posts as posted. No image is described on any of them.

posts.situation: A top-level post, Sun 15 Nov 00:49Z. Nothing in the data shows what prompted it. The author follows the game and plays its market (card games-top-chicken-market).

sensitive: The "top" and "bottom" wordplay may carry a sexual second meaning. Sexuality is out of bounds even as a reference (R10). The two quote posts listed read first as rank (top, middle, bottom). A third quote post, by an account with 315 followers, leans further on the second meaning and is left out. Also left out: three follow-ups by @shimmermathlabs.com. One quotes scripture (religion, R10), and all three reply to posts the digest hides, so what they answered cannot be given. "someday I will be Top Chicken" is its author's own statement that they have not won. The show names only winners in a ranking (R7, scorecard A10). Whether this post can be shown at all is for the reviewer, and it must not be turned into a forecast about its author. "bottom chicken" names nobody. No post here names anyone as a non-winner except its own author. @thebadcode.com's winning post that day is out of bounds (see games-top-chicken-standings); only the reply is here. @shimmermathlabs.com is marked as shown in the previous episode. "</virtue-signal>" is as posted. The digest holds three of the eight replies; the other five are not in it.
